### Terrain

```python
class Terrain(xs: np.ndarray, ys: np.ndarray, z: np.ndarray, z_datum: float)
```

Ground heights on a regular UTM grid.

xs, ys are absolute UTM coordinates (same frame as the building meshes);
z[row, col] is the height at (xs[col], ys[row]) in metres above z_datum,
the lowest point of the grid.

## Aerial photos (NAIP)

NAIP aerial photos for the ground and the roofs.

NAIP (USDA National Agriculture Imagery Program) is public-domain, ~0.6 m/px,
north-up imagery of the continental US. The USGS ImageServer reprojects it into
our UTM zone on request, so pixel (row, col) maps linearly to UTM (x, y).

Roofs in NAIP rarely sit exactly on the OSM footprints (georegistration error
and building lean away from nadir), so one shift for the whole area is found by
matching footprint outlines to image edges. Buildings stay on the OSM
footprints; only the roof texture is sampled at the shifted position.

Module `naip.naip` · [source](https://github.com/Qualcomm-MDP/PSM/blob/main/src/naip/naip.py)

### Ortho

```python
class Ortho(
    image: np.ndarray,
    west: float,
    north: float,
    res: float,
    roof_dx: float = 0.0,
    roof_dy: float = 0.0,
    ground: np.ndarray | None = None,
)
```

North-up aerial photo on the UTM grid.

image is RGB uint8 with row 0 at the north edge and column 0 at the west
edge; each pixel is res metres square. ground is the same photo with the
roofs painted out. A roof at UTM (x, y) appears in image at
(x + roof_dx, y + roof_dy).

| Field | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | `np.ndarray` |  |
| `west` | `float` |  |
| `north` | `float` |  |
| `res` | `float` |  |
| `roof_dx` | `float` | `0.0` |
| `roof_dy` | `float` | `0.0` |
| `ground` | `np.ndarray \| None` | `field(default=None, repr=False)` |
| `width_m` | `float` |  |
| `height_m` | `float` |  |

[source](https://github.com/Qualcomm-MDP/PSM/blob/main/src/naip/naip.py#L47)

Where the roofs, shifted by (dx, dy) metres, cover the image grid.

[source](https://github.com/Qualcomm-MDP/PSM/blob/main/src/naip/naip.py#L149)

### estimate_roof_offset()

```python
def estimate_roof_offset(
    image: np.ndarray,
    mask: np.ndarray,
    res: float,
    search_m: float = ROOF_SEARCH_M,
    reporter: Reporter | None = None,
) -> tuple[float, float]
```

Shift (dx, dy) in metres east/north that best lines roof outlines up with image edges.

Scores every shift up to +-search_m at once with an FFT cross-correlation
of x-edges with x-edges and y-edges with y-edges. A best shift at the edge
of the search window is probably spurious, so (0, 0) is returned then.

[source](https://github.com/Qualcomm-MDP/PSM/blob/main/src/naip/naip.py#L186)

### camera_position()

```python
def camera_position(x: float, y: float, terrain=None) -> np.ndarray
```

Camera centre in projection space: CAMERA_HEIGHT_M above the ground.

[source](https://github.com/Qualcomm-MDP/PSM/blob/main/src/texturing/tex_projection.py#L27)

### apply_textures()

```python
def apply_textures(
    mesh: trimesh.Trimesh,
    mapillary_data: dict,
    bbox,
    remove_obs: bool = True,
    seg_model: str | None = None,
    seg_device: str | None = None,
    image_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    max_saved_images: int = 12,
    reporter: Reporter | None = None,
    terrain=None,
    aerial=None,
) -> trimesh.Trimesh
```

Project street photos onto the mesh.

If image_dir is set, the first max_saved_images photos are also saved there
as small JPEG previews (original and, when obstruction removal runs, cleaned),
with an index in images.json.

If terrain is given, each camera sits CAMERA_HEIGHT_M above the ground at
its position instead of above z = 0.

If aerial (a naip.Ortho) is given, roofs are textured from it instead of
from street photos.

[source](https://github.com/Qualcomm-MDP/PSM/blob/main/src/texturing/tex_projection.py#L77)

## Progress display

Module `common.ProgressMonitor` · [source](https://github.com/Qualcomm-MDP/PSM/blob/main/src/common/ProgressMonitor.py)

### ProgressMonitor

```python
class ProgressMonitor(verbose: bool = True)
```

Monitor and track progress through a series of tasks.

**Example**

>>> monitor = ProgressMonitor(verbose=True)
>>> monitor.add_task("Load data")
>>> monitor.add_task("Process data")
>>> monitor.add_task("Save results")
>>>
>>> while not monitor.is_complete():
>>>     # Do work...
>>>     monitor.next()

Initialize the progress monitor.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verbose` | `bool` | Whether to print progress updates to console. |

[source](https://github.com/Qualcomm-MDP/PSM/blob/main/src/common/ProgressMonitor.py#L4)
